what_its_for: Liothyronine is a thyroid hormone used to treat hypothyroidism, a condition where your thyroid gland does not make enough thyroid hormone. It may also be used to treat or prevent certain types of thyroid goiters (enlarged thyroid) and is sometimes used in the diagnosis or treatment of thyroid cancer. This medicine helps your body have the right amount of thyroid hormone it needs to work properly.
how_to_take: Take liothyronine by mouth exactly as your doctor tells you. You can take it with or without food, but try to take it the same way each time. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Try to take it at the same time every day to keep a steady level in your body. Do not stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first, even if you feel well.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly increase it over time to find the right dose for you. The dose is different for each person and depends on your age, weight, medical condition, and lab test results. Most adults start with 25 micrograms (mcg) once a day. Your doctor may increase your dose every 1 to 2 weeks as needed. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are not sure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist for guidance.
storage: Store liothyronine tablets at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep the medicine in its original container with the lid tightly closed. Store it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine after the expiration date printed on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking antacids, calcium supplements, iron supplements, or cholesterol-lowering medicines like cholestyramine within 4 hours of taking liothyronine, as they can prevent your body from absorbing it properly. Avoid starting new medicines, vitamins, or herbal supplements without checking with your doctor or pharmacist first, as many products can interact with liothyronine. Avoid drinking large amounts of coffee or high-fiber foods right around the time you take your dose. Do not suddenly stop taking this medicine.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you have chest pain, fast or irregular heartbeat, shortness of breath, excessive sweating, severe headache, feeling very hot, shaking or tremors, or signs of a serious allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing. Also call your doctor if you notice symptoms of too much thyroid hormone such as feeling nervous, anxious, irritable, having trouble sleeping, losing weight without trying, or having diarrhea. Contact your doctor if your symptoms do not improve or get worse.
when_it_works: Liothyronine starts working faster than some other thyroid medicines. You may begin to notice some improvement in symptoms such as less fatigue or feeling less cold within a few days to a couple of weeks. However, it may take several weeks for your thyroid levels to fully stabilize and for you to feel your best. Your doctor will do regular blood tests to check your thyroid levels and make sure the medicine is working correctly.
special_populations: Older adults: Older patients may need to start on a lower dose because they are more sensitive to thyroid hormones and have a higher risk of heart-related side effects. Your doctor will monitor you carefully. Pregnant or breastfeeding women: Tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Thyroid hormone is very important during pregnancy for the baby's development. Your dose may need to be adjusted during pregnancy. Liothyronine passes into breast milk in small amounts but is generally considered safe during breastfeeding. Always check with your doctor. Children: Doses for children are carefully adjusted by weight and age. Children need regular monitoring to make sure growth and development are normal.
